12713: God declaring someone in the right, as in a law-court; in Galatians this includes being recognised as a true member of God's covenant family, able to share the table. Legal and covenant senses overlap.
12716: Trust, faithfulness, loyalty, allegiance. Can describe our reliance on Christ and possibly Christ's faithfulness to God.
12718: God's unmerited favour, the opposite of effort.
12719: A gift that creates a relationship and calls forth gratitude and loyalty. Paul stresses God gave it to people with no qualifying worth.
12721: Royal good news: the announcement that God's promised King has come, died and risen; also used of imperial announcements. Isaiah's herald of good news lies behind it.
12724: Abraham's promised offspring. Paul reads the singular as pointing to the Messiah, in whom many become one family and heirs.
12726: A schoolteacher who leads us to Christ.
12727: A household slave who supervised a boy until adulthood: walking him to school, guarding his behaviour, sometimes disciplining him. His role ended when the boy came of age. Not a teacher.
12729: A warm feeling of being God's child.
12730: A legal act in Roman society that made someone a full heir with the family name and property; Paul blends it with Israel's identity as God's son.
12733: Probably the basic elements and powers that ancient people believed governed the cosmos (earth, air, fire, water, and the heavenly bodies linked to calendars and gods). Paul puts both pagan religion and life under the law, in the old age, under this heading. Meaning debated.
12736: Human life in the old age, apart from God's Spirit, including religious pride in marks on the body (circumcision) as well as selfish desires.
12739: God's renewal of the world that has begun in the Messiah, echoing Isaiah's new heavens and new earth. Individuals share in it, but the phrase is cosmic.
12741: The church, which has replaced Israel.
12742: Disputed: the whole people of God in Christ (Jew and Gentile), Jewish believers in Jesus, or the Jewish people for whom Paul prays mercy.
